briefs.teaser: AI agents began trading investments and writing prescriptions this week, while a US court limited how far the government can pressure AI firms.
This week AI's biggest players struck multi-billion dollar deals to lock up computing power and open-source platforms, even as they warned that AI-driven cyberattacks are about to escalate.
Nvidia's blockbuster quarter and a wave of fresh AI investment collided this week with new evidence that most businesses are still not seeing a return.
AI's centre of gravity is shifting from buying models and chips to building and controlling them.
This week's AI news is about infrastructure and control rather than new chatbots, from shared agent standards to custom chips and government subsidies.
This week's AI news was about economics rather than breakthroughs, with falling model prices, a consolidating AI services market and shifting chip valuations.
Money is following AI off the screen and into robots, chips and orbital data centres, while security and staffing questions catch up with the software side.
Money is pouring into AI faster than ever, from Anthropic's soaring revenue to Nvidia's billion dollar model deal, even as the industry's own leaders admit the public does not trust it.
AI's commercial buildout kept accelerating this week, from chip deals to cheaper agent tools, even as evidence mounted that leading labs cannot yet fully control or audit what they have built.

This week's AI news was about control: Google, Anthropic and OpenAI all rolled out new admin, building and privacy tools for business customers, while a Pennsylvania order and a critical security flaw both aimed to rein in AI's downsides.
AI dealmaking accelerated this week, with Stripe, Etched and Higgsfield all closing deals worth billions while agentic tools spread into airlines, shops and payroll.
Anthropic proved a frontier AI lab can turn a profit, while hospitals, delivery apps and engineering firms pushed AI further into everyday operations.
AI's cost reckoning has arrived, from steep price rises and a new spending watchdog at EY to record sums flowing into the infrastructure that keeps it all running.
AI moved from lab to street this week: robotaxis scaled up in Europe, model makers cut prices again, and Beijing unwound a major AI acquisition.
This week's AI story was capital and control: $65bn changed hands in three deals while new standards bodies raced to keep enterprise AI in check.

This week's AI story was capital: Nvidia lined up $500 billion in financing, Anthropic alone signed over $15 billion in deals, while a KPMG survey found half of firms are already pulling back on AI agents over cost.

AI competition is shifting from model launches to who controls deployment, as ChatGPT passes a billion weekly users, Anthropic lines up a landmark IPO, and a security breach exposes thousands of firms running AI in production.
AI enters its production phase this week: enterprises are running it live, investors are pouring in record sums, and regulators have started enforcing their first binding rules.
